title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 13–15): Grothendieck is determining the endomorphisms of the profinite fundamental groupoid of the thrice-punctured sphere X = P^1 − {0,1,∞} (which is M_{0,4}) that fix a chosen set of base points and commute with the S_3-symmetry. He works with several partial groupoids, labelled II, III and IV, and glues them. On p.13 the two-vertex groupoid IV on the poles P^± gave the parametrisation (46) u(d) = d·φ(β) and the single condition (47) β·τ_∞(β) = 1. This has the shape of the 2-cycle relation f(x,y)f(y,x) = 1 of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group GT.

This page sets up a finer model, the groupoid induced on 11 vertices.
- R_i^ω (6 vertices): two points on the real circle, one on each side of each puncture i ∈ {0,1,∞}.
- Q_i (3 vertices): one point on each real interval.
- P^ω (2 vertices): the centres of the upper and lower half-planes.

There are three packets of edges, each a torsor under S_3, so 6 edges per packet.
- a_i^ω: the upper and lower half-circles around puncture i, joining R_i^+ and R_i^-.
- c_i^ω: real segments from Q_i to the adjacent R's.
- d_i^ω: meridians from the poles P^ω to Q_i.

Cell count: V − E + F = 11 − 18 + F = 2 gives F = 9. Three faces are the punctured discs. The other six are pentagons P–Q–R–R–Q–P. They give six relations forming one S_3-orbit, which is (48): (d_{ωi}^{ω'})^{-1}(c_{ωi}^{ω'})^{-1}(a_{ωi}^{ω})^{-1} c_i^ω d_i^ω = 1. As a check, the free groupoid on 18 edges and 11 vertices has rank 8; removing 6 relations leaves rank 2, which is π_1 of the 3-punctured sphere.

Complex conjugation τ (49) fixes the real vertices R and Q and swaps P^+ with P^-. It sends a^ω to (a^{ω'})^{-1}, fixes the real segments c, and swaps d^+ with d^-.

(50) rigidifies each vertex group as a copy of the standard Π_{0,3}, via isomorphisms φ_i^ω (at R), ψ_i^ω (at Q) and ψ̃_i^ω (at P). (51) expresses ψ and ψ̃ through the φ by transport along d and c (conjugation by the path). (52), together with (53) on the next page, records how the S_3 and conjugation symmetries act on these rigidifications, through the automorphisms σ_∞ and ε_0 of Π_{0,3}.

Purpose (realised on p.15): an S_3-equivariant, vertex-fixing endomorphism is given by u(a) = a·φ(λ), u(c) = …η…, u(d) = …ζ…, with λ, η, ζ ∈ Π̂_{0,3}, subject to (48). Instead of grinding through (48), he uses a van Kampen-type covering of the 'universal' groupoid by II and IV with intersection III. This yields the compatibility conditions (55): α̃ = η^{-1}ε_0(λη) = ζρ^{-1}(ζ^{-1}). These are proto-GT equations for the action of Gal(Q̄/Q), or of more general 'Teichmüller' symmetries, on the fundamental groupoid of M_{0,4} with real and tangential-like base points.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. (48) is consistent with a pentagonal cell decomposition (6 relations, one S_3-orbit, leaving a free group of rank 2).
In (49) the machine transcription gives τ(c_i^ω) = c_i^{ω'}. The image and the geometry indicate τ(c_i^ω) = c_i^ω, since the c are real segments fixed by conjugation.
The 'deux' inserted before 'relations' is doubtful. Geometrically there are six relations forming a single S_3-torsor, written as one schematic relation (48).
On p.15 the edges are called b_i^ω, while here they are c_i^ω. This is a notational inconsistency in the manuscript.

ideas.what: S_3- and complex-conjugation-equivariant cellular presentation of the fundamental groupoid of P^1−{0,1,∞} on 11 base points (real points near punctures, real midpoints, poles of the half-planes), with pentagonal relations
ideas.modern_name: Fundamental groupoid of M_{0,4} with several (real/tangential) base points; equivariant cell decomposition of the 'Teichmüller groupoid' in genus 0
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse, 1984) in spirit; base-point groupoid formalism developed by Ihara, Drinfeld (1990), Nakamura, Schneps, Lochak
ideas.where_published: The Esquisse d'un programme discusses Teichmüller groupoids with base points at a general level; this explicit 11-vertex presentation is not published as far as I know

ideas.what: Rigidifying each vertex group by isomorphisms with a standard Π_{0,3} and relating them by path-transport and S_3 symmetries
ideas.modern_name: Transport isomorphisms / trivialisation of the vertex groups of a groupoid

ideas.what: Parametrising equivariant groupoid endomorphisms by elements (λ, η, ζ) of Π̂_{0,3} and obtaining conditions by gluing sub-groupoids (van Kampen cover II ∪ IV, intersection III), leading to GT-type equations such as β·τ_∞(β) = 1
ideas.modern_name: Derivation of Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type relations (2-cycle, 3-cycle) at the M_{0,4} level
ideas.where_published: The Esquisse only sketches the idea that the tower of Teichmüller groupoids in levels ≤ 2 determines the Galois action

missed.claim: Grothendieck derives GT-like defining relations directly from an explicit S_3 × conjugation-equivariant presentation of the M_{0,4} groupoid. The base points include the two half-plane centres and real points around each puncture. The conditions come from gluing sub-groupoids, not from braid/associator relations. This is an independent, pre-Drinfeld route to the 2-cycle-type relation, here with group-valued parameters (λ ∈ Π̂_{0,3}, not merely in Ẑ*).
missed.quote: (48) (d_{ωi}^{ω'})^{-1}(c_{ωi}^{ω'})^{-1}(a_{ωi}^{ω})^{-1}c_i^ω d_i^ω = 1 ... L'automorphisme τ est donné par (49)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historically, it documents that Grothendieck had worked-out, equivariant base-point computations anticipating Drinfeld/Ihara's GT. Mathematically it is a known-type computation; specialists in GT (Schneps, Lochak, Nakamura) would recognise it rather than find new results.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a careful but essentially routine presentation of a fundamental groupoid with symmetry. Its interest is historical: the explicit, unpublished machinery Grothendieck used to reach GT-type equations before Drinfeld. There is no result here absent from the modern theory.
transcription_corrections: (49): τ(c_i^ω) = c_i^ω (not c_i^{ω'}); τ fixes R_i^ω and Q_i and swaps P^ω with P^{ω'}.

Header text: 'C'est le groupoïde engendré par ces sommets, les arêtes a_i^ω, c_i^ω, d_i^ω (trois paquets, chacun un torseur sous S_3) et les relations'. The insertion above 'relations' is unclear and may not be 'deux'.
(50): first line is Π_{0,3} → π(R_i^ω) via φ_i^ω; the struck-out continuation is '→ π(…'.
Line before (51): 'reliés par le fait que les relations suivantes, qui les expriment (les ψ_i^ω, ψ̃_i^ω) en termes des φ_i^ω'.
(51): second relation reads c_i^ω ψ_i^ω(g) = φ_i^ω(g), with conjugation by the path c implied.
